phase: Phase 5 slice 2 - H3-C, the topology sub-hypothesis of H3 (Structural Representation)
objective: Does DIRAC-S's pre-fusion visual representation retain topology-predictive information when the topology vector is withheld at inference, more so than the parameter-matched CNN/ViT baselines?
note: This is NOT gate_reports/gate_5.json. Gate 5 covers H1-H5 plus the 5 ablations together. This file records H3-C's result for the eventual gate_5.json to aggregate. H3-A (geometry) and H3-B (relations) remain separate future slices of H3, not run here.

design.why_not_a_naive_single_probe: DiracModel.forward requires ph_vector (the real, gudhi-computed T(X)) as an argument; TopologyHead embeds it directly into z via fusion (model/fusion.py). A naive z -> T(X) probe would partially just test whether fusion preserved information it was handed directly, not whether DIRAC's structure helps it perceive topology from the image -- CNN/ViT never receive ph_vector at all, so that comparison would trivially favor DIRAC by construction. Caught and the two-condition design below adopted before any GPU spend.
design.C0_sanity_check: DIRAC's full official z (ph_vector fed in via TopologyHead+fusion, the normal forward pass). NOT the primary comparison -- exists only to confirm the fusion pipeline actually preserves the topology information it's given. CNN/ViT have no equivalent condition (they never receive ph_vector at all, at any point).
design.C1_official_comparison: Pre-fusion h, mean-pooled, never touches ph_vector at inference, for all three architectures: DIRAC = encoder.encode_hidden(x) pooled over tokens; CNN = encode_hidden(x) (Phase 4) pooled over the spatial grid; ViT = encode_hidden(x) (Phase 4) pooled over tokens.
design.C1_caveat_not_architecture_alone: C1 is inference-time side-channel-free, but NOT a clean architecture-alone test. jobs/pretrain_dirac_job.py's L_topology trains PHPredictHead on (psi, rho) against the real ph_vector as a stop-gradient target, and psi/rho trace back through the encoder -- DIRAC's encoder received an explicit topology-prediction training-time gradient that CNN/ViT's training recipe has no equivalent of at all (Phase 4 deliberately used only L_recon+L_masked, since L_struct/L_topology have 'no non-contrived CNN/ViT equivalent'). A DIRAC C1 win could reflect the architecture, the L_topology training objective, or both -- this experiment cannot separate them. C2 (train a DIRAC variant with L_topology removed entirely, not just the inference-time fusion injection) would be needed to isolate 'architecture alone', and belongs to a future ablation phase, not this evaluation of the already-locked DIRAC-S.
design.no_dirac_s_modification: N_DIRAC-S stayed 1,552,520 (Gate 0's locked count) throughout -- no retraining, no architecture changes, no hyperparameter tuning against this result, per explicit instruction.

target: compute_persistence_summary(X) (model/topology.py) -- the same, already-defined PH summary used throughout Phase 3, not a new target invented for this probe. 9 dims: [count, sum, max] per homology dimension H0/H1/H2, already log1p-transformed at the source (the fix from Gate 3's smoke run).
probe: Single Linear(dim_in, 9) per condition, MSE loss, Adam lr=1e-2, 300 epochs -- identical probe architecture/optimization/evaluation-metric across all four conditions, re-run at probe-training seeds 0, 1, 2 (SEED env var; the underlying frozen representations are deterministic and cached once, only the probe's own init/training differs across these seeds). The only thing that legitimately differs across conditions is each representation's native width (DIRAC h=64, DIRAC z=256, CNN h=288, ViT h=136), which is architecturally unavoidable, not a controlled-comparison violation.
split_policy: probe trained on train split (n=533), scored on val split (n=145); test split untouched (spec Section 24)

C0_dirac_z.note: sanity check passed -- all 9 dims significant at p<0.001, confirms fusion preserves the injected topology signal

checks.per_dim_pattern: Consistent across ALL FOUR conditions including the C0 sanity check: count/sum statistics are recovered well (R^2 0.4-0.93 for C0 and dirac_h; 0.32-0.72 for cnn_h/vit_h), max statistics are recovered poorly (R^2 near zero or negative for C1's three conditions; still positive but weaker for C0). The single longest-lived persistence feature per homology dimension appears intrinsically harder to recover from any pooled representation than aggregate count/sum statistics -- an architecture-independent pattern, not specific to any one model. Stable across all 3 probe-training seeds, not checked separately here.

status: Real, probe-seed-robust C1 gap for DIRAC (mean 0.711 vs CNN 0.565 / ViT 0.564, margin 0.123-0.158 at every seed tried) -- NOT yet meeting the stronger, more expensive bar of reproducibility across independently-retrained backbones
interpretation: Unlike H1 (near-null across the board), H3-C's official C1 comparison shows a real, non-trivial gap: DIRAC's pre-fusion h noticeably exceeds both CNN's and ViT's h, and comes close to DIRAC's own C0 sanity-check ceiling (mean 0.749) -- meaning DIRAC's encoder recovers almost as much topology-predictive signal without ever seeing the answer as it does when handed the answer directly. This is the first genuinely encouraging signal for the central DIRAC hypothesis found so far in Phase 5. Two distinct robustness questions, deliberately kept separate: (1) PROBE-TRAINING-seed robustness -- checked here, re-running only the linear probe (3 seeds: 0,1,2) on the same cached, deterministic representations. Result: robust. Macro-Spearman is tight for every condition (CNN std=0.0003, DIRAC-z std=0.0014, ViT std=0.0048, DIRAC-h std=0.0142 -- the largest, but still small relative to the gap), and DIRAC's margin over the stronger baseline is positive at every seed (0.123, 0.152, 0.158) -- not an artifact of one lucky probe initialization. (2) BACKBONE-retraining-seed reproducibility -- NOT checked here. The underlying DIRAC/CNN/ViT checkpoints were each trained exactly once (seed=0); whether independently-retrained backbones would reproduce this gap is a separate, much more expensive question. Per IMPLEMENTATION_SPEC.md, that full multi-seed replication ('re-run the critical Gate-5 experiments across >=3 seeds') is explicitly Phase 6's job, done once all of Phase 5 is complete -- correctly out of scope here. This C1 result should be read as: a real, non-trivial, probe-noise-robust finding, and a strong candidate for Phase 6's backbone-level replication, not yet a fully locked result.
next: H3-A (geometry) and H3-B (relations) remain, plus H2 (data efficiency), H4 (uncertainty), H5 (robustness), and the 5 ablations. This C1 result is a strong candidate for one of the 'critical Gate-5 experiments' Phase 6 re-runs across independently-retrained backbone seeds, once the rest of Phase 5 is scoped and done once.
